answer.note: The four ref files are identical and give no file-specific priority, so I chose by reading the code. radon/metrics.py (C) holds mi_rank at line 150, which maps the score to A, B or C at the 9 and 19 boundaries. Its docstring says A is above 19, B is above 9 up to 19, and C is 9 or below. The code is `chr(65 + (9 - score >= 0) + (19 - score >= 0))`, so check the boundary scores 9, 9.01, 19 and 19.01. I'd give metrics.py about 35 of the 60 minutes. That covers the docstring-versus-code check and the tests in radon/tests/test_other_metrics.py. I'd give radon/complexity.py (B) about 12 minutes as a comparison, since it holds the sibling letter-ranking logic. The remaining time goes to a quick look at raw.py (A), about 8 minutes, because it supplies the inputs to the score, and visitors.py (D), about 5 minutes, which looks unrelated to the grade mapping. I replaced D in the incoming handoff with B because I found no evidence that visitors.py bears on the thresholds. If the next reviewer prefers the original C and D pair, that is a judgment call. I did not run the tests.
